summary: Long-lived Go streaming session rotates API key mid-stream causing duplicated function calls on retry
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that long-lived streaming connections using the Go SDK intermittently produce duplicated external function/tool invocations when their org rotates API keys mid-stream (short lived credential refresh).

Impact:
- Several webhook endpoints received duplicate POSTs for the same logical function invocation.
- Side effects at customer backend (duplicate payments/events) observed in 3 of 47 sessions.
- Affects production traffic for a private customer in us-east.

Environment:
- SDK: redwood-go v1.14.3 (using streaming client)
- Auth: short-lived API keys rotated by customer's key agent every ~25 minutes
- Backend: HTTPS webhook with idempotency-token header expected
- Models: gpt-4o-mini and redwood-open-7B observed in traces

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Start a streaming chat session via Go SDK with function calling enabled and a webhook callback configured.
2) Let the stream remain open > 20 minutes.
3) Trigger a function/tool from the model during the period when the customer's key agent rotates the API key.
4) If the SDK attempts an automatic retry due to an intermittent 502/timeout during the rotation, webhook receives two POSTs for the same invocation.

Observed behavior:
- Duplicate webhook invocations with two distinct request IDs from our platform (two server-side retry attempts).
- The SDK logs show an auth rebind: "auth: refreshed credentials, reconnecting stream" immediately followed by a retry of the in-flight chunk that had previously triggered the function.
- Customer-provided webhook logs show first invocation completed then second invocation replayed ~1.2s later.

Expected behavior:
- Either the stream retry should preserve the same idempotency scope so the function/tool is only executed once, or the SDK should attach a per-invocation idempotency token that survives auth rotation and reconnects.

Relevant logs (redacted):
- sdk-go: INFO auth: token refresh initiated (reason=rotation)
- sdk-go: WARN stream: connection closed (code=1006, reason=EOF)
- sdk-go: INFO stream: reconnecting session-id=abc123 (resume=true)
- sdk-go: DEBUG funccall: sending tool-exec event (invocation_token=)
- webhook: POST /tools/charge 200 OK (idempotency-token: none)
- webhook: POST /tools/charge 200 OK (idempotency-token: none)

Additional context provided by customer:
- They rely on their vendor key rotation for security (keys rotate every 25 minutes).
- They do not currently pass an explicit idempotency token in tool call metadata because they expected the SDK/platform to deduplicate retries for streaming reconnects.

Customer impact: Potential duplicate financial events in production. They have temporarily disabled long-lived sessions as a mitigation which impacts product UX.

investigation_notes:
Summary of findings:
- Root cause appears to be interaction between SDK stream resume logic and the absence of a per-invocation idempotency token. On reconnect, the SDK replays the last outbound chunk which includes the function-call event; serving-runtime treats replay as a new request and forwards to webhook.
- Auth rotation leads to a short disconnect; the SDK's resume=true path does not attach a stable invocation id token or replay-ordinal metadata that the runtime can use to dedupe.
- This is more likely for long-lived streams where tokens expire mid-conversation and the customer rotates frequently.
Technical hypotheses tested:
- Forcing the SDK to include a deterministic per-invocation nonce across reconnects prevents duplicates (verified in local harness).
- Adding server-side dedupe by storing a short-lived invocation fingerprint _also_ prevents duplicates but adds write latency and storage overhead.
Logs/links:
- Serving trace: https://observability.redwood.ai/traces/stream-abcd-20260311 (internal)
- Repro harness: https://github.com/nimbushealth/repro-stream-rotation (customer repro)
resolution:
Workaround provided:
1) Short term: Customer to include an explicit idempotency-token in the tool call metadata from their application layer (uuid per logical function invocation) and have the webhook reject duplicates based on that header. Support provided sample patch for Go SDK to set metadata before invoking functions.
2) Medium term: We have created internal task INT-4421 to implement per-invocation idempotency tokens in the Go SDK stream resume path and to add optional server-side short-window dedupe.

Follow-up actions:
- INT-4421: SDK change to carry 'invocation-id' across reconnects and attach to outbound function events (assigned to eng streaming team).
- Add integration test that simulates auth rotation during in-flight function calls.
- Customer to test provided SDK patch in staging and report results.

Customer acceptance:
- NimbusHealth confirmed they will test the provided patch in staging and accept the workaround for now. Support requested update when staging validation completes.
notes_for_followup: - Prioritize INT-4421 in the streaming sprint; this issue has potential for high-impact duplicates for customers with short rotation policies.\n- Ensure server-side dedupe design includes configurable time window and storage budget.\n- Update docs: recommend always attaching per-invocation idempotency tokens for webhooks when using long-lived streams under frequent key rotation.
